871.title: index.config.json: what this checkout instantiates
871.content: Skill index-config: index.config.json at an instantiation root says which harnesses the checkout instantiates, where each one comes from (local, or a remote mount pinned to a SHA), each layer’s config INLINE in its entry (a legacy <name>.config.json is only imported until --inline retires it), and which harness / is. Covers instantiated against declared, landing resolution and its error case, index.lock.json and its legacy fallback, the reserved index stem, the generated .gitignore block and its gate, and index-config:migrate (with --inline) for separated repositories. Named by: Subscribe to an external knowledge graph, Remote-mount a dependency . The schema is folio-index-config/v1 in cat-harness/schemas/kg/index-config.ts. The index is the ONE config. Each layer’s config is written inline in its instances[] entry. A <name>.config.json is a legacy file: imported only as a migration step, then retired with index-config:migrate --inline --write. Never create one — not to make a tool find a recipe, not for a new layer. If a reader only finds config in the file, that reader is the bug; fix it to read the index entry first. index.config.json holds three facts about how a checkout is instantiated: which harnesses are instantiated, which one is / (a checkout has one <base>/index.html), and where each one comes from, so each is stated once rather than spread across every root config. When it exists at the root it is authoritative. When it is absent, readers fall back to the root *.config.json files, their site.landing flags, and remoteMounts on the root declaration. { "$schema": "folio-index-config/v1", "instances": [ { "name": "folio-assistant", "source": { "local": { "at": "." } } }, { "name": "cat-harness" }, { "name": "my-ig", "source": { "remote": { "repository": "owner/my-ig", "ref": "<40-char sha>", "overrides": { "my-ig": { "whole": true } }, "trust": { "consent": { "...": "..." } } } } }, { "name": "my-guide", "contentType": "document", "site": { "build": { "sourceSteps": ["site:document"] } } } ], "site": { "landing": "cat-harness" } } .

872.title: Instantiated is a different fact from declared
872.content: A declaration (<name>.json) says what a layer declares. It travels with the harness into every checkout that uses the harness. An index.config.json entry says the layer is instantiated in this checkout. Without an index, a <name>.config.json at the root says the same thing. Tiles, the landing and the hub listing are all drawn from the instantiated set, which instantiatedHarnessNames(root) returns. Never derive that set from declarations or from a directory listing. The dependencies of an instantiated harness are not instantiated just because a mount’s closure brought them in. They keep a group of their own rather than disappearing. A harness that a KG subscription chose is instantiated the same way: kg:instantiate adds its entry, with its config inline, when the checkout has an index (and only without one writes a root <name>.config.json).

873.title: Inline, over a legacy import while one remains
873.content: Each entry’s effective config is built like this: . | Start from a legacy imported file, while one remains. That is import when it is given, else <name>.config.json, and only if the file exists. The target state is that no such file exists. | Overlay every other key of the entry (everything except name, import, source and _comment) as an inline HarnessConfig field. Objects merge key by key, and arrays and scalars are replaced. Inline fields win. | . effectiveInstanceConfig(root, name) computes it. readHarnessConfig(dir) returns it for any layer that an index lists, walking outward from the layer root and stopping at the first directory that holds either the index or the layer’s own config. A layer the index does not list is read from its own config file. Readers that are handed a root and a name (the site recipe in build-instance-site.ts) use readInstanceConfig in cat-harness-tools/scripts/instance-config.ts, which reads the same way and REPORTS every legacy file it reads. Retiring the files is index-config:migrate --inline --write: each imported file is folded into its entry by exactly the overlay above, so no effective config changes, and the file is deleted. index-config:inline:check fails while one remains.

874.title: Local or remote
874.content: . | source absent: local, at <name>/. | source.local.at: local, at that path. Use . for the layer declared at the root. | source.remote: a remote mount. It is a remoteMounts entry minus harness, which is the entry’s name. It reuses RemoteMountSchema instead of restating it, so it has ref (not pin), overrides.<name>.whole and .path, note, trust.consent and track, and every field added to RemoteMountSchema arrives with no edit here. | . There is one read path and one write path for remote mounts: . | Read: readDeclaredMounts(instanceRoot) returns the index’s remote entries when an index exists, else the declaration’s remoteMounts. If both carry mounts it throws and names both files. It never picks one. | Write: writeDeclaredMounts(instanceRoot, mounts) always writes index.config.json, seeding the index from the checkout first if there is none. It refuses while the declaration still carries remoteMounts. Nothing writes remoteMounts on a declaration. | .

875.title: Which harness / is
875.content: resolveLandingInstance(root) is the only reader. It applies these rules in order: . | condition | / is | . | the index is unreadable | invalid: the gate fails. There is no fallback to the flags, because the index was written to override them | . | the index’s site.landing names a layer it lists | that layer (by: "index") | . | the index’s site.landing is "hub" | the neutral hub: the harness listing and the todo panel | . | the index’s site.landing names a layer it does not list | invalid: the gate fails, and it is never a silent fallback | . | no site.landing (or no index), one layer | that layer (sole) | . | no site.landing, several layers, exactly one config flags site.landing: true | the flagged one | . | several flagged | the hub | . | none flagged | ambiguous: check:landing-instance fails, because the answer is never guessed | . | nothing instantiated | none: a state of its own, not a default | . gen-landing-data.ts and sync-docs-harness.ts ask this resolver. They do not use their own location. check:landing-instance also checks that the index and the root *.config.json files agree: . | A root config that the index does not import fails the check: without the index it would instantiate a harness, with it it does not, and nothing picks between them silently. | An import that names a missing file also fails the check. | An entry with no config file at all is the target state, and passes. | A legacy file an entry still imports is reported every time. It passes while it is a pending migration (every key it holds is either not inline or inline with the same value). It fails when the entry overrides one of its keys with a different value: the file’s value is then dead text that a reader of the file alone takes for the config. | .

876.title: A harnessed repository runs its checks on its own pull requests
876.content: Instantiating a harness in a repository includes turning its checks on there, through one reusable workflow the harness owns, never a copy per repository, so a layer is judged on its own pull requests and not only when an index re-pins it. Switching off a repository’s builds must not switch off its gates. The workflow is the tools layer’s .github/workflows/layer-pr-checks.yml. A repository calls it from a workflow of about fifteen lines that runs on pull_request: . jobs: checks: uses: <owner>/<tools-layer>/.github/workflows/layer-pr-checks.yml@main with: mode: layer # or `index`: the repository is its own index instance: <instance> # layer mode: its directory in the folio-assistant index path-in-repo: <instance> # where the instance sits in the repository ('.' at the root) . | layer mode is for a repository that an index mounts, such as cat-harness or the DAK layer. The workflow checks out folio-assistant and puts the PR in place of the locked mount. | index mode is for a repository that is its own index: an IG repository over the DAK layer, smart-ra, or a folio. Its own index.lock.json is replayed. | The gates are the harness’s graph checks over the repository’s own layer, plus every check:* / *:check script of that layer and its whole dependency harness (its transitive needs). Each is named <owning-instance>:<script>. | A PR fails only on what it newly breaks. Each gate and test runs on main and on the PR. Anything already red on main is listed, never hidden, and never counted against the PR. | . A layer PR that declares a new directory is red on two index gates it cannot clear. The index README lists every declared directory, so the PR leaves index:render:check and readme:sync:root:check stale, and only the index re-pin that takes the PR regenerates the README. Read those two as expected when they are the only new failures, and run them green in the index re-pin instead. Disabling a repository’s automatic builds is not disabling its checks. When an IG repository’s automatic gh-pages or IG Publisher triggers are switched off (the onboarding question in the FHIR IG layer’s ig-build-pipeline), the harness caller stays on.

877.title: The exemptions of the index’s own workflows
877.content: .github/workflows/ belongs to the index, so the steps CI runs there that the local gate set does not are exempted HERE, under gateExemptions.steps, each with a kind and a reason (GateExemptionsSchema, the same shape an layer declaration carries). They land in the same change as the workflow step, never ahead of it in a layer: an exemption for a step CI does not yet run matches nothing, and gates-workflows.test.ts refuses a stale exemption as it refuses an unclassified step. "gateExemptions": { "steps": [ { "match": "bun run cat state:push -- --id health", "kind": "ci-only", "reason": "…" } ] } . A layer still exempts its OWN scripts and steps in its own declaration.

878.title: index.lock.json, and the legacy name
878.content: The lock records what the declared mounts resolved to. It is generated by mount:remote and kept as a separate file. The legacy name is <root-instance>.mount-lock.json. The rules for each reader and writer: . | Writers write index.lock.json. mount:remote first renames a legacy lock onto the new name, so the old file is moved, never dropped. | Readers take index.lock.json first, then fall back to the legacy *.mount-lock.json, so downstream folios and old branches still replay. The readers are: . | mount-from-lock.ts | mountedInstanceRoots | mountedUnder in git-corpus.ts | mount:remote:check | . | Both files present is an error that names both. Two locks are never merged. | . mount-from-lock.ts imports only node:*, so it restates the rule inline and its test holds it to lockFilesIn. A re-pin ends with one commit per layer, and moves pins only forward (owner ruling, 2026-11-06, card “Pin target”, A). Every layer the change needs is pinned in the same re-pin, and the re-pin PR holds the pins and nothing else: a change that needs the new pins stacks on it (owner ruling, 2026-11-07). The one exception is a change mutually dependent with the re-pin, where neither passes alone. It may share the PR, and the body says why. The rules are in remote-mount §”Re-pinning”.

879.title: The reserved index stem
879.content: index.config.json ends in .config.json, so a scan that treats “each root *.config.json is a harness” would find a harness called index. The index stem is therefore reserved across the board: . | rootConfigStems skips every index.* file. It is the one root scan; every other reader calls it or instantiatedHarnessNames. | findDeclarationFile skips every index.* file too. | The index schema refuses a layer named index, and hub, because that is the landing keyword. | . Do not add another copy of the scan: a new copy is how the reserved name leaks back in.

880.title: The generated .gitignore block
880.content: # BEGIN index mounts (generated from index.config.json — do not edit) /my-ig/ # END index mounts . The block holds one /<path>/ line per remote layer in the index, where the path is overrides.<name>.path, else <name>/. After those it lists every further layer root the lock records, because a mount’s closure can land layers that the index never names. Three things write the block: . | mount:remote | writeDeclaredMounts | index-config:migrate --write | . check:index-ignores fails when the block is missing or disagrees with the index. When an index exists, mount:remote does not append to .git/info/exclude: a local exclude rule is invisible to every other clone, so a path the committed block does not cover is reported as not ignored. Without an index, it still appends there.

881.title: Converting a checkout: index-config:migrate
881.content: bun run cat index-config:migrate # print the index it would write, and its findings bun run cat index-config:migrate --write # write it; move remoteMounts; write the block; rename the lock bun run cat index-config:migrate --check # exit 1 when --write would change anything (a gate here) bun run cat index-config:migrate --inline --write # also fold each <name>.config.json into its entry, and delete it bun run cat index-config:inline:check # exit 1 while any imported <name>.config.json remains bun run cat index-config:migrate --root <clone> # a separated repository's standalone checkout . The converter reads only the files under --root, so it runs on a standalone clone of any separated repository. | Which root configs it imports: a root <name>.config.json is imported only when name is a layer the checkout declares (at the root or one level down) or mounts. Anything else becomes an unmatched-config finding and is not imported. A repository cut from a fork, for example, can carry the fork’s own <fork>.config.json; importing it would instantiate a harness the repository does not hold. | Re-runs: it is idempotent. A re-run moves only the remoteMounts entries that the declaration has gained since the last run. An entry the index already holds identically is dropped from the declaration. An entry the index holds differently throws, and you reconcile it by hand. | .

948.title: translations — status
948.content: The gettext side of the translation-sources graph, measured from the files in cat-harness/translations. Every number here is derived on each run; none is written down. Governed by the translation-manager skill. These numbers last changed on 2026-11-13. Question 1 (Availability): Are there .po catalogues for extractable .pot templates? Question 2 (Completeness): Of the catalogues that exist, how many strings are translated? Question 3 (Officiality): Has a person signed this locale off? Read from the PO headers and status.json, which must agree. Scroll horizontally to see all columns → . | locale | catalogues / templatesQ1: availability | entriesQ2: strings | translated | fuzzy | untranslated | officialQ3: signed off | . | ar Arabic | 15 / 11013.6% · view files → | 734 | 68593.3% | 0 | 49 | not signed off (machine or agent translation) | . | es Spanish | 15 / 11113.5% · view files → | 735 | 68693.3% | 0 | 49 | not signed off (machine or agent translation) | . | fr French | 16 / 11314.2% · view files → | 767 | 71893.6% | 0 | 49 | not signed off (machine or agent translation) | . | ru Russian | 15 / 11013.6% · view files → | 734 | 68593.3% | 0 | 49 | not signed off (machine or agent translation) | . | zh Chinese | 15 / 11113.5% · view files → | 736 | 68793.3% | 0 | 49 | not signed off (machine or agent translation) | .

949.title: folio-assistant-core
949.content: Measured from folio-assistant-core/translations, that instance's own translation-sources directory. Scroll horizontally to see all columns → . | locale | catalogues / templatesQ1: availability | entriesQ2: strings | translated | fuzzy | untranslated | officialQ3: signed off | . | ar Arabic | 6 / 3815.8% · view files → | 361 | 361100% | 0 | 0 | not signed off (machine or agent translation) | . | es Spanish | 6 / 3815.8% · view files → | 346 | 346100% | 0 | 0 | not signed off (machine or agent translation) | . | fr French | 6 / 3815.8% · view files → | 346 | 346100% | 0 | 0 | not signed off (machine or agent translation) | . | ru Russian | 6 / 3815.8% · view files → | 346 | 346100% | 0 | 0 | not signed off (machine or agent translation) | . | zh Chinese | 6 / 3815.8% · view files → | 361 | 35999.4% | 2 | 0 | not signed off (machine or agent translation) | . Two questions, not one. catalogues / templates asks whether a .po exists at all for each extractable .pot; the string columns ask how much of the catalogues that DO exist is done. A locale can be near 100% translated across a handful of catalogues while most of its templates have none — which is why the first column is not folded into the rest. “no basis” is not zero. A share over an empty denominator is undefined, and rendering it as 0% would report a measurement this run did not make. One directory per table, each named. translation-sources is a graph KIND, and more than one instance may declare it; the first table measures the directory named in the subtitle, and each instance below it gets its own table for its own declared directory. They are never summed: two instances' catalogues answer two questions. A catalogue sitting in an instance that has not declared the directory is invisible here — which is a gap in that declaration rather than a locale with no work done, and the two must not read the same. Fuzzy is counted apart from translated. A fuzzy entry has a translation and needs review; adding it to translated would flatter exactly the entries a reviewer must look at.

1277.title: Glossary
1277.content: Derived: every term this instance's swimlanes define — the role's title and description, the lane names that bind it, and whether the term has been retired. This is an index, not the documentation. It says what exists and what each artefact declares about itself. What a process is for, when you would be in it, and what it is not, is authored beside it and reuses these entries rather than restating them — see the auto-docs skill. Filter this table | Artefact | What it declares about itself | . | Activity logglossary-ledger.json | The agent activity log. A MECHANICAL role: it is written to at task start and task end, and emptied by an actor — one entry, all of them, or on a periodic sweep — and it decides nothing. Modelled on work-plan and corpus, the two existing stores; its skill is the contract it is held to. Its entries are held in the layer's unpublished store and never reach a published graph; the activity-log skill names the location, which is deliberately not repeated here because a role description IS published.notation role/logfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Actorbootstrap/glossary-ledger.json | no description in the artefactnotation process/Process_LogMessage/lane/Lane_Actorfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Adjudicatorglossary-ledger.json | Settles a criterion whose reviewer entries disagree, and records WHY. Inherits reviewer because an adjudicator is a reviewer with one added entitlement — the adjudication permission — and the separation is the point: a reviewer reports, an adjudicator settles, and a process where every reviewer could settle has no way to say who decided. 1343.content: Derived: every DMN decision table a declared `processes` graph holds, with the decision's own name. Sub-graph cat-harness/processes. This is an index, not the documentation. It says what exists and what each artefact declares about itself. What a process is for, when you would be in it, and what it is not, is authored beside it and reuses these entries rather than restating them — see the auto-docs skill. | core-processes folio-assistant-core/processes … | library-processes cat-harness/library/processes … | processes cat-harness/processes … | . | Artefact | What it declares about itself | . | Detangled?cat-harness/processes/kg/decisions/detanglement-gate.dmn | An unassigned column above zero means the measurement is incomplete. A low edge count over an unclassified corpus is the same false comfort as a green check over an empty one — and this rule is FIRST so no cross-edge count can outrank it. | . | Stands alone?cat-harness/processes/kg/decisions/isolation-gate.dmn | No declaration of its own: the directory moves and nothing downstream can resolve it. | . | Ready to seed?cat-harness/processes/kg/decisions/seed-readiness-gate.dmn | A PR marked as moving much of the tree is still open over this layer: the seed would snapshot one side of it. | . | Declared in place?cat-harness/processes/kg/decisions/subgraph-declared-gate.dmn | Could not determine. NOT "not yet" — a malformed declaration is a fault, and answering it with the convention would report a guess as an answer. | . | Is the sign-off recorded, and does it let the work proceed?cat-harness/processes/process/decisions/requirement-signoff-recorded.dmn | No attestation: the judgement was not written down, so nothing may follow it. | .

1361.title: auto-docs index
1361.content: Derived documentation over a declared sub-graph. Each entry below is generated from the repository on every build, so it is what the tree actually holds rather than what anybody remembered. These are indexes, not the documentation. They say what exists and what each artefact declares about itself. What a thing is for, when you would reach for it, and what it is not, is authored beside them and reuses these entries rather than restating them — see the auto-docs skill. | Decisions …every DMN decision table a declared `processes` graph holds, with the decision's own name | Docs …every AUTHORED documentation page an instance publishes, with the title and description its own front matter declares | Processes …every BPMN process, with its own documentation, its lanes, and the skills its activities name | Roles …every role a declared `scenarios` graph defines, with the description it declares | Schemas …every schema module a declared `schemas` directory holds, with the first sentence of its module docblock | Skills …every skill markdown file, with the description it declares in its own front matter | Tasks …every named activity in a declared `processes` graph — task, user, service, manual, script and call activities | Tools …every Tool module a declared `tools` directory holds, with the first sentence of its module docblock | .

1365.title: The catalogue, as a graph
1365.content: The replica pages show what IRIS looks like. This one shows what this catalogue knows — and, more usefully, what it records that it does not know. The gap is the point, not a backlog. This instance models 235 node(s) against 273,559 items across 1,057,223 files upstream. Cataloguing by reference means recording that something exists without holding it, so a small number here is the design rather than a shortfall.

1411.title: Strict, advisory — and nobody said
1411.content: Three states, not two. loadProcessModel reads an undeclared policy as strict, which is right for the engine — “a process that forgot to say is governed, not exempt” — and hides a fact a reader wants. Somebody chose strict and nobody said, so the engine assumed strict are different, and the second is 19 of 94 here. | enforcement | declared | defaulted | . | strict | 44 | 19 | . | advisory | 31 | 0 | .

1412.title: Findings
1412.content: Every one of the 94 diagrams has a rendered SVG. Activities carrying no <bootstrap.processes:skill ref> — a census, not a gap list . 40 across 22 diagram(s). This section reported them as defects in its first version, and that was wrong: beans luke and uuhu worked this corpus from 90 down to this remainder and settled what is left. luke: “coverage is deliberately NOT gated — a human sign-off step has no skill”. uuhu added the call-activity exemption and recorded that its own remainder “are not gaps”. 15 are call activities, which delegate to a subprocess — the skill is named there, and naming it twice would be one fact in two places. The other 25 are listed by lane, because the lane is what says whether a person, a pipeline or an agent performs the step, and only the last of those has a skill to run. | lane | steps | . | Agent | 7 | . | Stakeholders | 4 | . | Contributor | 2 | . | Owner | 2 | . | Agent (playing the machine) | 1 | . | Board renderer | 1 | . | Build pipeline | 1 | . | Content Author | 1 | . | Editor / author (person) | 1 | . | Folio-Assistant Agent | 1 | . | Publication manager | 1 | . | Requestor | 1 | . | Reviewer | 1 | . | Reviewer / SME | 1 | . No verdict is offered on which of these is a gap, and that is the honest state rather than a hedge: distinguishing a person’s judgement step from an agent step somebody forgot needs the lane’s actor KIND, which a free-text lane name does not give — process-model.ts notes sixty lanes spell two dozen positions. The lane’s partitionElementRef is the join that would answer it, and it is present on 25 of these 25 steps — which is the measurement, not an impression. An earlier draft of this sentence said few of these and was counting whether the lane had a NAME, a different question with a different answer.

1452.title: Apply a vocabulary mapping table
1452.content: Carry one source record into a target vocabulary by a declared folio-vocab-mapping/v1 table: each source field becomes the predicate its row names, in the table’s order, with a DERIVED target (such as dcterms:title rendering skos:prefLabel) copied from its authoritative one so the two cannot drift. A table is shaped like a FHIR ConceptMap: an existing ConceptMap, R4 or R5, is representable as one without loss (fromConceptMap), and a table can be produced as a ConceptMap (toConceptMap), which returns every loss rather than dropping anything silently. First consumer: glossary-export. |   |   | . | Tool | vocab-map | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/vocab-map.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/vocab-map/vocab-map.json | . | invoked | inProcess | . | qa | qa-reports | .

1461.title: Skills it satisfies
1461.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. kg-separation . Separate a Knowledge Graph into its own repository — as a CONTENT repository (files to read, no code) and a TOOLS repository (the code that writes and checks it) — once it is too large, or its consumers or cadence differ. The end-to-end method: the signals that trigger it, the preconditions, eleven stages each with the command that gates it, the owner’s decision points, how identifiers, QA and publication move, how the parent consumes the result, rollback, and the post-move sweep that a move between the pair owes before the parent re-pins. graph-detanglement owns stages 1–3; this skill owns the rest. Bootstrap + bootstrap-tools and cat-harness + the tools layer are the worked examples. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/graph-management/kg-separation.md. Also satisfied by: mount-from-lock, package-exports, rewrite-moved-paths, separation-cutover-check. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/kg-separation/{input,output}.schema.json). kg-affordances . The four affordances of a conformant knowledge graph — browse, materialise, instantiate and copy-into-folio — which capabilities each requires, how each writing verb degrades cleanly when no write capability is available, and how copying an asset stamps KgAsset.source provenance. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/kg-affordances.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/kg-affordances/{input,output}.schema.json).

1493.title: Check that an ArchiMate model’s fhir-actor tags point at the IG’s FHIR ActorDefinitions
1493.content: Actors come first: the IG’s ActorDefinitions are written from the DAK’s personas, and an ArchiMate model only points at them. For one model a layer’s cat-archimate.config.json names, this reads every element carrying the Archi property fhir-actor, whose value is an ActorDefinition’s canonical URL, and the IG’s ActorDefinitions: FSH InstanceOf: ActorDefinition under input/fsh/, and FHIR JSON under fsh-generated/resources/ or input/resources/, each canonical being <sushi-config canonical>/ActorDefinition/<id> unless its url says otherwise. It fails on a value that is not a canonical URL, a tag that names no ActorDefinition, an element kind that cannot be an actor (a data object, a goal), and a type mismatch (a #person actor on an application or technology element, a #system actor on a business actor or role). It warns about each ActorDefinition no element realizes; --strict makes that a failure. --json prints element → actors and actor → elements, for page back-links. It never writes an ActorDefinition or any FSH, and never matches boxes to actors by name. |   |   | . | Tool | archimate-actors | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/archimate-actors.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/archimate-actors/archimate-actors.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

1667.title: Skills it satisfies
1667.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. repo-conversion . Lay folio-assistant over a repository that already exists, without losing or silently moving what is in it. Scans the tree read-only, classifies candidate files into library (external source) and content (authored here) with an explicit third bucket for what it cannot classify, scans outside the content tree for mathematical evidence and refutations, lists the content markers (an IG, a DAK, processes, work items, library, Lean, folio manifests) the harness could declare and declares only the ones the person picks, puts the three questions the scan cannot answer to the author as selections, and hands ingestion to one agent or a small swarm. Use when a user wants an existing repo converted to a folio, asks to import what is already there, asks whether their PDFs/notes/drafts can come along, or asks what else in a repository an existing harness could declare. Source: cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/repo-conversion.md. Also satisfied by: instantiate-harness. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/repo-conversion/{input,output}.schema.json). getting-started . Triage what a person means when they ask to create a folio, and route them. Five requests share one sentence — a folio in a new repo, folio-assistant overlaid on an existing repo, a second folio in a layer that already has one, a content object they called a folio, or something the filesystem cannot tell apart. Reads the repository facts, runs them through the folio-intent decision table, asks a selectable question for what facts cannot settle, scaffolds, and reports the published URL. Use whenever a user asks to create, start, set up, or initialise a folio, a paper, a DAK, an IG, or “folio-assistant” itself. Source: cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/getting-started.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/getting-started/{input,output}.schema.json). folio-init . Scaffold a new folio layer from the harness — the instantiate affordance of the knowledge graph. Covers when to run folio-init vs remote-mount, what the scaffold writes, the builder shim, state branch seeding, write capability requirements, and –dry-run degradation. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/folio-init.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/folio-init/{input,output}.schema.json).

1675.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. kg-separation . Separate a Knowledge Graph into its own repository — as a CONTENT repository (files to read, no code) and a TOOLS repository (the code that writes and checks it) — once it is too large, or its consumers or cadence differ. Bootstrap + bootstrap-tools and cat-harness + the tools layer are the worked examples. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/graph-management/kg-separation.md. 1724.title: Publish a built site to gh-pages as a full replace
1724.content: Lay a built _site onto a gh-pages checkout as a FULL REPLACE and push it, keeping the open pull requests’ staging previews: each attempt re-reads the branch, re-runs restore-staging and keep-shared-payloads against what is on it now, replaces the tree, commits docs(gh-pages): site from <sha> and pushes. A rejected push is rebuilt, never rebased (a rebase would re-apply the replace over a preview a sibling just deployed), up to three attempts. A restore that cannot read the branch stops the publish. A site that matches the branch is a no-op, not a failure. 1748.title: The render pipeline, in dependency order

1789.title: Mount remote harnesses at a pinned commit, only when trusted
1789.content: Lay down each declared remote mount — a source.remote layer in the root index.config.json, or, in a folio with no index, a remoteMounts entry on its declaration (both at once is refused) — and its dependency closure, from another repository at a full commit SHA. Write the lock, index.lock.json (a legacy <name>.mount-lock.json is read, and renamed onto it when rewritten), and, with an index, regenerate the root .gitignore block that ignores each mount path. It READS the declared mounts and never writes them: a tool that changes a mount writes through writeDeclaredMounts into index.config.json. Before anything is checked out, each mount must pass the trust gate (schemas/kg/mount-trust.ts, rule H8): a person’s consent recorded for THIS pin, or a signature in a declared trust network. No signature verifier exists yet, so a signature alone is could-not-determine and does not mount. Unsigned and unconsented is refused. --staging mounts for a preview and needs neither. A directory id an override or mountDefaults names may be one the layer declares in its <name>.json or one it declares FROM WITHIN a declared directory (skills/skills.json naming voices), resolved at the pin through instanceDirectories; an id in neither is refused at plan time. tools on an override names Tools by id and mounts each one runnable: its definition (<tools dir>/<id>/<id>.ts), its implementation (the inProcess.module, or the script its bun run cat <key> resolves to) and their import closure, walked by bootstrap-tools’ importClosure (the one closure walker), as every declared directory that closure touches — the lock still records directories only. A hydrated mount lays each chosen directory down as its published index.hydrated.jsonld only: read from the pin’s git tree when a commit carries it, otherwise fetched from the pin’s subgraph index package (the subgraph-index-<sha> release asset subgraph-index-package publishes), its tarball checked against its folio-binary-release/v1 record, its manifest against the repository, pin and harness asked for, and each file against its sha256, SubgraphHydratedSchema and the subgraph IRI; the lock records the package’s URL and sha256 so a replay fetches the same bytes. --check compares the disk against the lock and never fetches. When a run CHANGES the lock, it then re-renders the agent surface (skill:commands → .claude/commands/, agent-memory → .claude/agent-memory/ and .agents/) from the checkout root, so a re-pin commit carries the skills and memory the new layers define; a generator that fails fails the run, and --no-agent-surface opts out. |   |   | . | Tool | remote-mount | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/remote-mount.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/remote-mount/remote-mount.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

1806.title: Where to drop a file — the queue’s upload URL
1806.content: Compose the forge URL a person can drop a file at, from the layer’s own declaration: the uploads graph’s directory, resolved against the ROOT its scope names, expressed relative to the repository, and appended to the origin remote as GitHub’s /upload/<branch>/<path>. Every failure is NAMED and no URL is guessed — no declaration, no declared uploads graph, a declared queue absent from disk, no origin remote, and a non-github.com remote each return a reason and a remedy instead. The declared path is relative to the LAYER and a forge URL needs it relative to the REPOSITORY, so pasting the declared path can mint a 404. |   |   | . | Tool | upload-url | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/upload-url.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/upload-url/upload-url.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

1807.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. upload-routes . How a file actually REACHES uploads/ — the two mechanisms that write bytes into a declared queue, the persona that performs one of them on somebody’s behalf, and what each writer owes that the route does not do for them. Getting a resource INTO the graph in the first place — accepting one offered unprompted, or asking for one and then asking for it to be uploaded. The channels are plural and open: uploads/ is one, the conversation is another. Runs before document ingestion, which begins only once a file has landed. Source: cat-harness/library/skills/library-core/content-acquisition.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/content-acquisition/{input,output}.schema.json).

It also answers “which queue” when a checkout declares more than one (one per layer): the answer is whichever layer root you pass, never a literal. | . | limits | It answers WHERE, and nothing else. 1835.title: Instantiate a harness over a repository that has none: pin, mount, open the setup-only PR, render the preview
1835.content: The scripted step of the initiation process (getting-started.bpmn, the repo-conversion skill §4). Reads the harness’s declaration at its pin and every needs, transitively (a need beside the layer that needs it unless –repo-of says otherwise, at its default branch’s tip unless –pin says otherwise, its declaration’s name checked), seeds them all into the repository’s index.config.json with the consent given (remote-mount --seed --whole), sets site.landing to the harness, site.agentRun and mountApprovers, mounts the closure (remote-mount: index.lock.json and the .gitignore mounts block), installs it as root workspaces with the hoisted linker, writes the root bootstrap (.github/cat.ts and .github/mount-from-lock.sh from cat-harness-tools templates/root-bootstrap/) and sets the root’s cat script to bun .github/cat.ts, so bun run cat … mounts the layers itself on a later fresh clone, re-renders the agent surface from the mounted generators, runs the harness’s instantiate:<harness> checkout script when a mounted layer declares it, and commits on a branch (default harness/). Then, unless --local, pushes the branch, provisions gh-pages when absent (`pages-bootstrap --provision`), opens the setup-only PR, runs `prepare:` when declared (what the site is built from and nobody commits, such as an IG's AST) and renders the branch's preview at gh-pages branches// (`stage-local`); with --local the site is built and composed and nothing is pushed. It imports only node:*, so it runs from a fresh clone of cat-harness-tools before anything is mounted: it lays the platform's own closure, at the pins the repository will mount, into a temporary root to run the mount from. On a repository with nothing mounted yet, run the same file from a fresh clone: `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness-tools /tmp/cht && bun run /tmp/cht/scripts/instantiate-harness.ts …`. Two more flags, not declared as ports because no constrained type carries them yet: `--pin =` pins one layer of the closure, `--repo-of =<owner/repo>` says where a need lives. |   |   | . | Tool | instantiate-harness | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/instantiate-harness.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/instantiate-harness/instantiate-harness.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

1836.title: Skills it satisfies
1836.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. repo-conversion . Lay folio-assistant over a repository that already exists, without losing or silently moving what is in it. Scans the tree read-only, classifies candidate files into library (external source) and content (authored here) with an explicit third bucket for what it cannot classify, scans outside the content tree for mathematical evidence and refutations, lists the content markers (an IG, a DAK, processes, work items, library, Lean, folio manifests) the harness could declare and declares only the ones the person picks, puts the three questions the scan cannot answer to the author as selections, and hands ingestion to one agent or a small swarm. Use when a user wants an existing repo converted to a folio, asks to import what is already there, asks whether their PDFs/notes/drafts can come along, or asks what else in a repository an existing harness could declare. Source: cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/repo-conversion.md. Also satisfied by: folio-init. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/repo-conversion/{input,output}.schema.json). remote-mount . Bring a harness, and every layer it depends on, into a checkout that does not hold it, from another repository at a pinned commit, as declared directories with a lock: a source.remote entry in the downstream’s root index.config.json (legacy: remoteMounts on its declaration) and mountDefaults on the harness. Covers when to mount and when to subscribe instead, why there are no submodules and no .deps/, the transitive closure through needs and gitlinks, overrides by id, the lock, and the three states. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/remote-mount.md. Also satisfied by: build-instance-site, index-config-migrate, kg-retrieve-npm, mount-from-lock, npm, subgraph-index-package. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/remote-mount/{input,output}.schema.json).

1885.title: Lower the tangles in ArchiMate views: re-route lines and swap same-size boxes in a row
1885.content: Searches for a less tangled drawing of each view: a line may be re-routed straight or orthogonally (an L, or a Z through a free lane between boxes), and two same-size boxes in the same parent and row or column may swap places. A change is kept only if it lowers crossings + lines through boxes + lines drawn on top of each other. Without --apply it reports before and after per view; with it, the model is written back in place, only the moved boxes’ bounds and the re-routed lines’ bendpoints changing. |   |   | . | Tool | archimate-detangle | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/archimate-detangle.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/archimate-detangle/archimate-detangle.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

1886.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. archimate-models . ArchiMate models as knowledge-graph content: how a layer declares the Archi models it holds, what the archimate subgraph gives every model, view, element and relationship (an IRI, a thin page, and every view drawn as SVG from the model’s own diagram, and its metamodel derived and checked), how to version the models, how to wire them into a folio’s staging build and navbar, how to count and lower the crossed lines in a view before committing it, why every view carries a plain-language key, why names are the source’s own terms linked to their SKOS concepts, and why no Java, no Archi CLI and no Archi HTML report is ever part of the pipeline. Read before adding, authoring, publishing or rendering an .archimate file, before citing an ArchiMate element from prose, and before reaching for Archi’s own tooling in CI. 1918.title: Screen a hand-over for injected instructions, field by field
1918.content: Before a model reads a sub-agent’s report, a delegated prompt, a tool result or a comment from someone who is not the principal, screen it against a declared schema whose top-level fields are control (steers what the receiver does) or data (content it reads). A finding in a control field, or any field the strict schema does not declare, is REFUSED, so a report cannot extend the delegator’s plan. A finding in a data field is QUARANTINED: the original is kept and marked, never stripped. The patterns are a deterministic tripwire (instruction overrides, role and turn spoofs, fence breaks, tool-call syntax, hidden Unicode, exfiltration links, pipe-to-shell), a mitigation and not a guarantee. 1935.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. kg-separation . Separate a Knowledge Graph into its own repository — as a CONTENT repository (files to read, no code) and a TOOLS repository (the code that writes and checks it) — once it is too large, or its consumers or cadence differ. Bootstrap + bootstrap-tools and cat-harness + the tools layer are the worked examples. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/graph-management/kg-separation.md. 2096.title: Convert a checkout to a root index.config.json
2096.content: Write the root index.config.json (folio-index-config/v1) that says which layers the checkout instantiates, where each comes from (source.local or source.remote) and which owns / (site.landing), from the root *.config.json files and the declaration’s remoteMounts. With --write it moves remoteMounts off the declaration into source.remote entries, writes the generated .gitignore block, and renames a legacy <name>.mount-lock.json to index.lock.json. Without a flag it prints the index it would write. Idempotent: a re-run merges what the declaration gained, and refuses an entry the index already holds differently. A root config naming no layer is reported as unmatched-config and not imported, because what to do with it is a person’s decision. |   |   | . | Tool | index-config-migrate | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/index-config-migrate.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/index-config-migrate/index-config-migrate.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

2210.title: Build, check and (on request) publish a layer’s own site, or a branches/ preview
2210.content: From a checkout whose layers arrive by remote mount: mount the pinned closure, install, run the layer’s own gates (--pre), compose the harness chrome for THIS layer, run its source steps, build with Jekyll at the base path read from the git remote (/<repo>, or /<repo>/branches/<branch> for a preview), run the post-build steps (mount-instance-docs, pdf-viewer, set-html-lang, publish-id-lookup, rail-standalone-pages), and check that every relative or base-rooted link in every page resolves to a file under the site, reading each page with an HTML parser. Any failing step stops the run; a link that does not resolve means nothing is published. 2261.title: Is this repository’s cutover from the monorepo complete? Measured, condition by condition
2261.content: Run in a separated repository. Six conditions, each decided by an existing gate: mounts (every declared layer on disk at its pin — remote-mount --check), declarations (every path a declaration names resolves — declaration-resolution), monorepo-paths (no wiring still names the monorepo: livesAt on it, a submodule of it, a reusable workflow called from it, a path into its old checkout — the one condition implemented here), import-direction and reference-direction (no layer reaches a layer above it), and site (the site builds from the mounts alone, every link resolving — build-instance-site --no-mount, only with --site). Findings inside a MOUNTED layer are listed and not counted: a defect in a layer pinned from upstream is fixed upstream and re-pinned. Exit 0 complete, 1 a condition failed, 2 a condition could not be determined or was not run — without --site the answer is never 0. |   |   | . | Tool | separation-cutover-check | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/separation-cutover-check.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/separation-cutover-check/separation-cutover-check.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

2312.title: Skills it satisfies
2312.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. archimate-models . ArchiMate models as knowledge-graph content: how a layer declares the Archi models it holds, what the archimate subgraph gives every model, view, element and relationship (an IRI, a thin page, and every view drawn as SVG from the model’s own diagram, and its metamodel derived and checked), how to version the models, how to wire them into a folio’s staging build and navbar, how to count and lower the crossed lines in a view before committing it, why every view carries a plain-language key, why names are the source’s own terms linked to their SKOS concepts, and why no Java, no Archi CLI and no Archi HTML report is ever part of the pipeline. Read before adding, authoring, publishing or rendering an .archimate file, before citing an ArchiMate element from prose, and before reaching for Archi’s own tooling in CI. Source: cat-harness/skills/ui/ui-core/archimate-models.md. Also satisfied by: archimate-actors, archimate-blocks, archimate-check, archimate-detangle, archimate-metamodel, archimate-pages. 2394.content: Rewrite every third-party uses: owner/repo@ref outside the declared staging-only workflows to @<full commit SHA> # <ref>, so Dependabot keeps the pair current. A tag resolves to its PEELED commit (an annotated tag’s object is never pinned), else a branch head, by git ls-remote with argv. A ref that resolves to nothing, or to more than one commit, is refused and reported, never guessed. This repository’s own reusable workflows are first-party and left alone. 2468.title: Skills it satisfies
2468.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. sub-kg-lifecycle . A sub-KG is a knowledge graph staged as a directory inside a harnessed repository, declared as its own layer, that may later leave for a repository of its own. The lifecycle: declare it in place, grow it, stage it for separation (one import seam, the separation guard, a self-contained rehearsal), and then, each behind an explicit owner confirmation, create the repository, copy the staged contents in with history, re-point the declaration, verify on a fresh clone and delete the in-repo copy. The light sibling of kg-separation: use this for a DATA layer that leaves whole, and kg-separation when a graph must split into a content repository and a tools repository. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/graph-management/sub-kg-lifecycle.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/sub-kg-lifecycle/{input,output}.schema.json).

2492.title: Publish a folio’s or an IG’s site from the agent’s own checkout — the one agent publish path
2492.content: Build a repository’s site in the agent’s checkout and push it to the publish branch, as a preview or as the main site, without an Actions runner. Which build is read from the repository: a declared site.build recipe (built by build-instance-site), else the reusable workflow its own workflow files call — folio-staging.yml for a folio, the WHO SMART Base IG’s ghbuild.yml for a FHIR IG, whose build job is planned step by step and run as written. For an IG it then applies the harness chrome over the built output (sync-docs-harness, then rail-standalone-pages --foreign-site --instance <the IG>): every page gains the rail and the icon row #fa-navbar-row, and the IG’s own content is left byte for byte. A root publish is REFUSED when the chrome cannot be applied, and a clean root deploy is refused over any root whose index.html wears the icon row unless the new output does too, so a chromed root is never replaced by bare IG Publisher pages. Every run prints its plan first, and the plan lists the chrome step; --plan stops there, --dry-run composes the commit in a temporary worktree and pushes nothing, --artifact writes a claude.ai Artifact bundle instead. |   |   | . | Tool | stage-local | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/stage-local.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/stage-local/stage-local.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

ArchiMate models as knowledge-graph content: how a layer declares the Archi models it holds, what the archimate subgraph gives every model, view, element and relationship (an IRI, a thin page, and every view drawn as SVG from the model’s own diagram, and its metamodel derived and checked), how to version the models, how to wire them into a folio’s staging build and navbar, how to count and lower the crossed lines in a view before committing it, why every view carries a plain-language key, why names are the source’s own terms linked to their SKOS concepts, and why no Java, no Archi CLI and no Archi HTML report is ever part of the pipeline. 2606.title: Skills it satisfies
2606.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. archimate-models . ArchiMate models as knowledge-graph content: how a layer declares the Archi models it holds, what the archimate subgraph gives every model, view, element and relationship (an IRI, a thin page, and every view drawn as SVG from the model’s own diagram, and its metamodel derived and checked), how to version the models, how to wire them into a folio’s staging build and navbar, how to count and lower the crossed lines in a view before committing it, why every view carries a plain-language key, why names are the source’s own terms linked to their SKOS concepts, and why no Java, no Archi CLI and no Archi HTML report is ever part of the pipeline. Read before adding, authoring, publishing or rendering an .archimate file, before citing an ArchiMate element from prose, and before reaching for Archi’s own tooling in CI. Source: cat-harness/skills/ui/ui-core/archimate-models.md. Also satisfied by: archimate-actors, archimate-blocks, archimate-check, archimate-crossings, archimate-detangle, archimate-pages. For one model a layer’s cat-archimate.config.json names, this reads every element carrying the Archi property fhir-actor, whose value is an ActorDefinition’s canonical URL, and the IG’s ActorDefinitions: FSH InstanceOf: ActorDefinition under input/fsh/, and FHIR JSON under fsh-generated/resources/ or input/resources/, each canonical being <sushi-config canonical>/ActorDefinition/<id> unless its url says otherwise. It fails on a value that is not a canonical URL, a tag that names no ActorDefinition, an element kind that cannot be an actor (a data object, a goal), and a type mismatch (a #person actor on an application or technology element, a #system actor on a business actor or role). It warns about each ActorDefinition no element realizes; --strict makes that a failure. --json prints element → actors and actor → elements, for page back-links. For each figure under figures that names an svg, writes the view as SVG (the same drawing as the view’s page). 2633.title: Check a review log and its repository’s issues for changes
2633.content: The mechanical check a review-log watcher runs on every poll. Given a drafting sheet’s Contributor Feedback values and the folio repository, it reads the repository’s open and closed issues (leaving out pull requests, issues labelled no-sheet and, with --author, issues someone else opened) and compares a digest of them and of the cells people set (Title, Selected Sections, Contributor Feedback, Disposition, Ready for agent, Ready for merge, Dispositions confirmed; on a public-comment log also Committee Feedback, TWG (CS), TWG (human) and Change Set (human)) with the last check’s. Unchanged: it prints {"status":"unchanged"} and exits 0. Changed: it exits 10 and lists what changed (issue opened, updated or closed; a cell’s old and new text), the Contributor Feedback rows to append, one per issue that no row’s Issue cell links yet (Title the issue’s title, the first Contributor Feedback column @login (#N): first paragraph, Issue the issue’s URL; a closed issue’s row marked closed), and closedRows, the rows linking a closed issue, which the watcher hides with their text struck through. A read with no Issue column (a public-comment log’s Review Change Sets) tracks only issues labelled change-set unless --label says otherwise, and appends no rows: each open issue is reported as an issue-unlinked change instead. It writes no sheet and no issue: the watcher appends the rows and does the agent pass. With --accept it stores the new state for the next poll to compare against. |   |   | . | Tool | review-log-watch | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/tools/review-log-watch.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/folio-assistant-core.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | folio-assistant-core | . | source | folio-assistant-core/tools/review-log-watch/review-log-watch.ts | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

2649.title: Folio review coverage
2649.content: Compute the two facts content-change-review.bpmn’s coverage gate (GW_Covered) reads: uncoveredBlocks, the changed blocks with no reviewer verdict on their CURRENT hash, and openDefects. 2650.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. review-comments . Reviewer comments on a folio’s edit-set, from a tagged pull-request comment to a structured todo on the review page. Covers the tag a reviewer types, how the comments are ingested into review-comment/1.0.0 todos, where the published review-comments.json comes from and when it refreshes, how a comment follows a renamed block and survives a removed one, who may change a comment’s status, and how to change this process. Use when a reviewer asks how to comment on a block, when the review page shows no comments or a wrong one, when editing the ingestion, or when a folio’s staging workflow is set up. Source: folio-assistant-core/skills/content/content-lifecycle-ext/review-comments.md. Also satisfied by: folio-review-comment-move, folio-review-comments. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/review-comments/{input,output}.schema.json).

2692.title: Spreadsheet tabular metadata
2692.content: Read a workbook into a folio-tabular-csvw/v1 record, one CSVW table per rectangular block of cells. Blocks are split on empty rows, then on empty columns, so several tables on one sheet are found, each anchored at its real top-left cell (fac:anchor: sheet, A1 cell, row, column). Dates are read through the number formats in styles.xml, not misread as integer serials. A malformed part is refused rather than half-read. Reads the ZIP with node:zlib and SpreadsheetML with fast-xml-parser. Governed by the tabular-metadata skill. |   |   | . | Tool | tabular-xlsx | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/tools/tabular-xlsx.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/folio-assistant-core.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | folio-assistant-core | . | source | folio-assistant-core/tools/tabular-xlsx/tabular-xlsx.ts | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

2724.content: Stage three of skill-pipeline-subject-indexing for MeSH: look up every candidate heading of a draft (a preferred heading, an entry term, or a descriptor id, with an optional qualifier) in NLM’s MeSH authority at id.nlm.nih.gov, current year. 2748.content: For every figure a source publication declares, report whether the folio built from it has a block and how computable it is: missing, excluded (signed off), picture (a PNG crop), linked (a picture linked to a model view), computable (a diagram, a table or a figure rebuilt by ArchiMate, BPMN, DMN, Mermaid, a class diagram or a generator), or cited (a picture kept on purpose, signed off). Turn a figure into a computable diagram: every figure of a source publication when a folio is built from its L1 entry, and any hand-drawn figure in a folio, an IG or a demonstrator that is redrawn from a source. 2756.content: The scoring step of the automatic-term-extraction method: count the word n-grams of one or more Markdown or text files (not across punctuation, front matter or code), and rank them by C-value as Frantzi & Ananiadou 1996 define it, so nested multi-word terms are not swamped by the longer phrases that contain them. 2772.title: ArchiMate model from the glossary
2772.content: Make an ArchiMate model agree with the instance’s folio-glossary/v1 terms whose focus is an ArchiMate element: elements matched by their skosConcept property (never by name) take the term’s prefLabel and definition, a term with no element gets one on no view, and the relationships the terms list are added. A type that disagrees is reported, never changed. A relationship between two linked elements that no term lists is reported, and removed with --prune along with the lines that draw it. No box or line is moved. Without --write it only reports; --check fails when anything would change. --seed goes the other way once, and only from an ingested model held under library/ (--from): an authored model is never a source of the glossary. |   |   | . | Tool | archimate-from-glossary | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/tools/archimate-from-glossary.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/folio-assistant-core.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | folio-assistant-core | . | source | folio-assistant-core/tools/archimate-from-glossary/archimate-from-glossary.ts | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

2844.title: Build the review sheet’s Apps Script and a document’s Config tab
2844.content: Builds Code.gs (--script), the one Google Apps Script every review sheet runs (from review-sheet.gs), and one document’s Config tab rows (--config), filled from the folio’s review/public-comment/sheet-sync.json, its review anchors and the draft’s pdf-line-map.json. The script keeps a public-comment review sheet’s links and joins current: each comment No. links to its comment page; Sections, Page and Line no(s) link to the page of the frozen review draft; Review Change Sets joins its comments, suggested revisions, feedback and dispositions, each No. n linking to its row; and on both tabs Agentic status lists each pull request of the change-set, linked, with its status and what it changed, from the Agent tab. It reads the document’s URLs, tab and column names and data from the sheet’s Config tab (visible, locked to the owner), which the agent writes from these rows. 2883.title: Tools
2883.content: As an API: OpenAPI document · MCP tool list · API reference. A skill states a capability generically: what an actor needs to know to perform a task. A Tool is one concrete way to exercise it, with an installation, an invocation and typed inputs and outputs. One skill may be satisfied by several tools, and one tool may satisfy several skills. They are separate graphs and this is the tools one. The relation between them is satisfies, and it runs from a tool to a skill — this tool is one way to do that, never this skill is a tool. 175Tool nodes 79skills satisfied 153invoked as a shell command 23reachable over MCP

2885.title: Who declares each specification
2885.content: A user declares the specification it depends on; the record names no user. That is data-modelling step 8 — the dependent holds the pointer — and it is why this list cannot drift from the code: a file that stops declaring stops being listed. Four forms are read: a @conformsTo tag, a conformsTo: front-matter list, an xmlns binding, and a graph typology whose typing module declares the spec (bean u63y). Every declaration names a record on this page. 2 record(s) nothing declares. A version bump would move nothing that says so: . | foaf | w3c-org | .

2886.title: Namespaces the corpus uses against the ones it declares
2886.content: Read from diagram files (BPMN and DMN), metadata records, and JSON-LD contexts — 33 namespace IRI(s) are in use across the corpus. Derived rather than listed, so an artefact that adopts a new vocabulary shows up here instead of going unnoticed. Every namespace the corpus declares is covered by a record above. 4 declared and not in use. Not a defect on its own: a record may cover a namespace only some artefacts carry. It is here because a registry nobody prunes is one that stops describing the repository. | http://www.w3.org/ns/formats/N-Quads | https://openprovenance.org/ns/provext# | https://spdx.org/licenses/ | https://www.omg.org/spec/DMN/20191111/DMNDI/ | .

2887.content: DCMI Metadata Terms . dcmi-terms — DCMI, edition 2020-01-20 — reads, meaning this repository parses documents written in it. Namespaces. | http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/ | http://purl.org/dc/terms/ | http://purl.org/dc/dcam/ | . Note. reads, not conforms: these records describe external metadata (DSpace), so a DCMI revision is a compatibility question rather than a migration. The transcription came first, which was the defect: dublin-core.ts was written from one captured IRIS record and carries the prefix string dc with no namespace URI and no edition, recording what one deployment spells rather than what the standard defines. A transcription with no cited edition cannot distinguish a missing field from one absent in that edition. The operative terms below are derived from the catalogue records, so they are what IRIS actually sends (DSpace also mints dcterms, local and other prefixes this repository has not met). A term absent here is undeclared, not unsupported. Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN) . omg-bpmn-2.0 — OMG, edition 2.0 — conforms, meaning this repository’s artefacts are valid against it. Namespaces. | http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/MODEL | http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/MODEL# | http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/DI | . Note. The 20100524 in every namespace is BPMN 2.0’s release date and is how the edition is identified in an instance document — the diagrams have carried it since the first one was drawn, and until 2026-09-20 nothing in this repository said which specification that was. conforms rather than reads: these are our instance documents, so a version bump is a migration of the corpus rather than a compatibility question. No XSD is held and none is fetched — referenced, per the owner’s “dont need to materalize, but should reference specific version being used”. That means nothing validates a diagram structurally against OMG’s schema; check:workflows and kg:audit check the things this repository cares about (lanes bind declared roles, activities name skills) and are not a substitute for it. The MODEL# form is the RDF spelling of the same namespace: OMG publishes no RDF vocabulary for BPMN, so a graph that states a sequence flow’s sourceRef/targetRef or a node’s incoming/outgoing (kg-export, and bootstrap-tools’ export-graph.ts) names BPMN’s own attribute by appending # to its XML namespace — the model’s name for the relation, rather than a second one minted here (owner, 2026-09-30, bean xsqm). That collision is exactly why a namespace URI is the identity here and a prefix is not.
